items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1973-08-06
items.q: I took Ben O' Kennedy quit his band, I took Ben O' Kennedy's place.

ctx.x: Why did you go on that train? You went to Wichita? No, no.

That was during the days of the, what do you call it, the Dixie Series. We used to have Texas and Louisiana, we played at the winners from each, and we were going to Dallas. That's where you first went? That's where we stopped. Those guys had me playing my horn all night on the train, Herschel and a few of the others. And that's when we got off to Dallas. That's where Herschel separated from me, went on with the T&T band. And I had Lucien and McCarthy, Richard. And we played at one of the roughest joints in…
Now what kind of band was that that you were there, with McCarthy and Jeff?

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1969-12-30
items.q: And the great trumpet player that was in his band, Ben O'Kennedy, quit Troy's band in Galveston... I got the job from just him and him... he became the first chair man

ctx.x: Well, tell me a little bit more about Troy Floyd's band. I don't know too much about it, it's what you've told me.

Well, the history of Troy Floyd's band goes way back to the days of Alfonso Trent, who was a band that was organized with Texas musicians and Arkansas, because Trent originally was from a little town of Fort Smith, Arkansas. His estate was still there, I visited the estate just a couple of three years ago. And Trent was playing at the Adolphus Hotel, incidentally the first name of a band to be put into one of these big establishments. So Troy had his band organized with mostly Texas men. And the great trumpet…
Well, how did he play then? Did he use many head arrangements? Would he just be faking all the time or what? I don't know.
